text:
Emily Chen: Heads-up — we had a customer hit a tail-latency spike when the tiling policy deferred to the low-cost GPU pool. Looks like requests were deferred multiple times and we hit client-side timeouts. Need a quick sync on how defer-on-slow should behave with timeouts and hedging. :worried:

Raj Patel: Oof. Can you paste the logs? My mental model: defer-on-slow should only trigger once per request decision, and we should attach a decision_id so downstream can correlate retries/hedges. If we don't, repeated defer + retry loops are possible.

Emily Chen: Logs snippet: ```
[2026-03-21T17:02:41Z] route_decision id=dcf8a8 defer_to=pool-low-cost reason=latency_est>=80th
[2026-03-21T17:02:41Z] request_forwarded id=dcf8a8 backend=pool-low-cost
[2026-03-21T17:02:46Z] timeout client_id=foo status=408 id=dcf8a8
```
Client retried immediately and got deferred again.

Olivia Gomez: Two concerns: (1) telemetry contract needs to surface the decision_id and the policy flags (defer_on_slow=true, probe_attempts=1) so we can build replayable traces; (2) the policy engine API currently has no notion of "defer TTL" — we need to avoid tight retry loops.

Alex Murphy: Proposal: add a per-decision "defer_window_ms" and emit decision_id + parent_request_id in telemetry. Behavior: when a request is deferred, we set a small cookie on the request path: {decision_id, expires_at}. Any retry with same parent_request_id within that window should avoid re-defer and instead fallback to hedged pool or immediate fallback.

Raj Patel: Tradeoffs:
- + reduces retry thrash and client timeouts
- - increases state we must carry on each request and requires consistent parent_request_id propagation across load balancers
- - hedging sooner may increase cost; need budget controls per-tenant

Olivia Gomez: For telemetry, we also want latency_histogram buckets (0-5ms,5-20,20-100,100-500,500+) and a boolean field "defer_hit" and string "decision_id". That lets Optimize map cost impact.

Emily Chen: Sounds reasonable. Quick question on implementation surface: should defer_window be enforced in the policy engine (centralized) or in the runtime sidecar (local, faster)?

Alex Murphy: My vote: runtime-sidecar enforcement with central policy providing the default. Reason: sidecar can check local cache quickly and avoid RPC roundtrips. Central controller can push policy updates (defaults, max_window).

Raj Patel: Agreed. Sidecar enforcement also lets us tie to connection/session-level IDs. But we must ensure TTLs are signed or HMACed to avoid tampering in untrusted environments (private deployments).

Olivia Gomez: Security note: for Private/VPC we can rely on network controls, but still HMAC the decision tokens. Also add a telemetry field "token_sig_ok".

Emily Chen: Minimal config example Alex suggested: ```yaml
policy:
  defer_on_slow: true
  defer_window_ms: 2500
  fallback_strategy: hedge-first
  emit_telemetry: [decision_id, parent_request_id, defer_hit, latency_histogram]
```

Alex Murphy: Experiment plan:
1) Roll sidecar change to canary (10% traffic) with defer_window_ms=2500 and hedge-first.
2) Capture telemetry and run a replay on synthetic retryy workloads.
3) If client timeouts drop and cost delta < 5% for test tenants, widen rollout.

Raj Patel: Add guardrail: per-tenant daily budget threshold to disable hedge-first automatically if cost > threshold. That avoids surprising bills.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: sidecar/0.12.3 -> canary (10%) starting 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z. Release notes: added decision token, defer_window enforcement, telemetry fields.

Emily Chen: Action items: @Raj add budget guardrail PR, @Olivia update telemetry schema + CI tests, @Alex prepare canary config and playbook for rollback. I'll run incident replay for the customer's trace and attach results here. :+1:

Raj Patel: I'll open PR today.

Olivia Gomez: Updating schema now, will link the PR.

Alex Murphy: Canary config in my repo: alex/tiling-defer-canary. Will ping when ready.

Emily Chen: Thanks everyone — let's regroup after canary metrics (48h).
